title: Polpette al sugo
subtitle: Italian meatballs braised in tomato sauce
excerpt: Polpette al sugo are the Italian meatball: a mix of beef and pork, shaped into walnut-sized balls, browned in olive oil, then simmered in a simple tomato sauce for 20 minutes. They are softer and more herb-forward than their American cousins. Serve on their own, or with pasta or polenta.
sourceNotes: Italian home-cooking tradition. Meatballs in tomato sauce are eaten across southern and central Italy, particularly Campania, Lazio, and Calabria. Method drawn from Marcella Hazan, Essentials of Classic Italian Cooking (1992).

recipe.freezeNotes: Meatballs in sauce freeze well. Thaw overnight and reheat gently over low heat.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the batch easily. Freeze in meal-sized portions.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Meatballs improve overnight in the sauce. Make ahead and reheat.

glossaryTerms.definition: Italian meatballs; the word applies to any size from small walnut-sized polpette to large palm-sized ones eaten as a main course rather than with pasta.

content.text: simmered in a straightforward tomato sauce. The meatballs are made with beef and pork, soaked bread for softness, Parmesan, and a little parsley. The bread is the key to a tender texture: dry breadcrumbs make a denser meatball, soaked bread makes a more yielding one. Brown them first so the tomato sauce doesn't wash out the colour.

items.prepNote: crusts removed, soaked in milk and squeezed dry

content.text: Mix {{beef-mince}} of beef, {{pork-mince}} of pork, the squeezed bread, egg, Parmesan, parsley, and grated garlic with salt. Mix until just combined; do not overwork. Roll into walnut-sized balls, about 3 cm across.
Heat {{olive-oil}} of olive oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Brown the meatballs in batches, turning to colour all sides, about 5 minutes per batch. Set aside.

In the same pan, cook the {{onion}} onion for 5 minutes. Add the sliced garlic for 1 minute. Add the tomatoes and passata. Bring to a simmer. Add the meatballs. Cover and cook for 25 minutes, turning once. Add the basil at the end and season. Serve with crusty bread, pasta, or polenta.

items.cause: Too wet, or mixture was overworked.
items.fix: Squeeze the bread very dry before adding. Handle the mixture minimally.

items.cause: Too much bread squeezed out, or egg proportion is low.
items.fix: The bread should be soaked until soft but still moist, not bone-dry.

content.text: Meatballs in tomato sauce are a home dish across southern Italy, eaten on their own with bread as a main course rather than with pasta. Serving them with spaghetti is an Italian-American tradition; in Italy, pasta and meatballs stay separate. These polpette are the standalone version: soft, herb-forward, and braised until the sauce is thick and dark.
